clue.text: Hunted animal in deep pit

definitions.meaning: the creature a hunter pursues is his prey
an open excavation from which stone is dug

explanation.surface: A hunted beast has gone to ground in a deep hole.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the prey being chased and a pit where stone is cut, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Unrealistic cox quit, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or unreliable, so the letters before it are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone guesses the rowing cox has given up, an idealistic move.
explanation.definitionFit: From Don Quixote, it describes impractical, idealistic schemes with no grip on reality.

clue.text: Fend off a check pinning rook

indicators.note: pinning means holding fast inside, so the chess piece is held within the check

parts.note: to vet something is to check it
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess player escapes a check that pins their rook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check' and 'rook' set a chess scene, but 'check' just means vet.
explanation.definitionFit: To ward off or prevent a danger is to turn it aside, a straight synonym.

clue.text: See 5
Signal to go south for vegetables

parts.note: a green light tells traffic to proceed

explanation.surface: An instruction to head south in search of vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun for leafy cooked vegetables such as cabbage, a common informal synonym.

clue.text: Give a severe warning that something has to stop a dictator there abroad

definitions.text: Give a severe warning that something has to stop

indicators.note: abroad means scattered far and wide, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Somebody overseas must stop a tyrant and is sternly warned.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was an old law read aloud to order a crowd to disperse.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from the 1714 Riot Act, read to unruly crowds; it now means to reprimand sternly.

clue.text: Former plot to get editor removed

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a tract is a plot of land

explanation.surface: An old conspiracy aims to have the newspaper editor ousted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a conspiracy, but it is a stretch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pulled out, like a tooth, has been taken out, a direct past participle synonym.

clue.text: Inferior rum imbibed by cast

indicators.note: imbibed by means drunk in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a shy is a throw, as at a coconut shy
rum is old British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Cheap rum drunk by the actors of a production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' and 'cast' suggest a drink and actors, but mean odd and throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Badly made, poor-quality goods are cheap and second-rate, a direct adjective synonym.

clue.text: Incendiary device and axe British gang brought over

parts.note: to axe someone is to sack or fire them

indicators.note: brought over signals that the British gang is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a mob is an unruly gang

explanation.surface: Someone smuggled an incendiary and an axe into Britain with a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' makes BOMB; 'axe' looks like a weapon in the scene but is the verb meaning dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapon designed to start fires is an incendiary bomb, the device named here.

clue.text: Work hard on bird book beforehand for famous publisher

indicators.note: beforehand says the book's letter comes in front of the bird

parts.note: to beaver away is to work hard
a rook is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: Toil over a bird book in advance for a celebrated publisher.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Beaverbrook was the Canadian-born press baron who owned the Daily Express.

clue.text: Play part in saving Oscar's operation

parts.note: to act is to play a part on stage

indicators.note: saving here means keeping safe within, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: taken as written
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An actor plays a role in a film that rescues Oscar's surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' gives ION; 'Oscar' suggests the film award, but is just the radio code word for O.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is a process in motion, as in 'the machine is in action', a fair synonym.

clue.text: Army entertainer

definitions.meaning: a large multitude, as in a heavenly throng
one who receives and entertains guests

explanation.surface: A soldier who entertains the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a great multitude, as in biblical hosts, and the person who receives guests.

clue.text: Innovative Reagan TV ad broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A groundbreaking television advert for Ronald Reagan goes out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived phrase describes art or ideas ahead of their time, pioneering and experimental.

clue.text: Text boss if he fails to give punishment

indicators.note: fails suggests the words collapse and break down, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Message the boss: if he flops, he gets disciplined.
explanation.walkthrough: SIX OF THE BEST is six strokes of the cane, once a British school punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a caning of six strokes, a traditional schoolboy punishment.

clue.text: Item number one raised protest

parts.note: an object is an item or thing

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, so the letters are turned round

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The first item on the agenda drew a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns NO + I round to ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Voicing disapproval or disagreement is lodging a protest, a direct noun synonym.

clue.text: Ordinary wine I must get imported, mostly red

indicators.note: imported means brought in, so the letter goes inside the wine

parts.note: Medoc is a red wine from Bordeaux

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: red taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A plain wine I have to bring in, chiefly a red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of RED to leave RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something average and unremarkable is second-rate and run-of-the-mill, a close synonym.

clue.text: Young man in job, scared on moving staircase?

indicators.note: moving means shifting about, so the letters are stirred into a new arrangement

parts.note: a lad is a young man
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young man, nervous in his job, rides an escalator.
explanation.walkthrough: The young man goes into the pool with JOB and SCARED. The question mark marks the definition as playful: Jacob dreamt of a ladder to heaven with angels going up and down it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the patriarch dreams of a ladder reaching heaven; the name is also given to steep ship's ladders, loosely a staircase.

clue.text: Money-spinner? Caught a cold when invested in gig

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a gig is a show or performance
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A performer caught a chill while backing a profitable concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' hints at finance, but just means set inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A business or product producing steady profit with little effort is milked like a dairy animal.

clue.text: Attract fish over to the sheltered side

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to draw is to attract
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Lure a fish across to the calm side of the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors use it for the side away from the wind, so it means toward the protected flank.

clue.text: Paint company on left of us

parts.note: our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: A paint firm is positioned to the left of us.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to tint or apply pigment is to paint; British spelling with u.

clue.text: Standard Shakespearean jester

definitions.meaning: a benchmark against which quality is judged
the fool in As You Like It bears this name

explanation.surface: A typical clown from one of Shakespeare's plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a criterion of quality, from the stone once used to test gold, and is the clown's name in As You Like It.

clue.text: Understand wife interrupting children's game

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: tig is the chasing game also called tag

explanation.surface: A wife breaks up the children's playtime.
explanation.walkthrough: TIG is the British name for the playground chasing game tag.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang: to twig something is to grasp or realise it suddenly.

clue.text: Sample some ragout, a stew

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Try a little of the ragout, which is a kind of stew.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample food is to try a little of it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Circular diagram, old, found in Cadiz, specially designed

indicators.note: found in says one piece is placed inside the other
specially designed means the letters of the city are rebuilt in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old circular chart discovered in the Spanish port of Cadiz, specially made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially designed' rearranges CADIZ to ZDIAC, and 'found in' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The astrological chart of the twelve star signs is drawn as a circle, so it is a circular diagram.

clue.text: Traveller's bag ultimately stuck down by fire

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: nap is the soft downy surface of cloth
to sack someone is to fire them

explanation.surface: A traveller's bag ends up glued down beside the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack carried on the back by hikers and travellers is a bag of this kind.

clue.text: Fame in future? Now none

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word across the second into the third

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that celebrity will not last into the future.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide recognition and celebrity is a direct synonym for being famous.

clue.text: A daughter at this point gives stick

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies
here means at this point or place

explanation.surface: A daughter at this moment hands over a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' looks like a noun handed over, but it is the verb meaning cling.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick to something is to cling fast to it, the verb's ordinary synonym.
